title: Real-valued SSMs not optimal for all modalities
description: The paper uses real-valued SSMs as the default, but these work well for all except one task (audio waveforms). The authors hypothesize that complex numbers are helpful for continuous modalities (audio, video) but not discrete ones (text, DNA), and note that the audio experiment required switching from real to complex parameterization.
canonical_description: real-valued state space models underperform on certain continuous perceptual modalities

evidence.anchor: work well for all but one of our tasks

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: Data is abundant (public audio/video/text/DNA benchmarks). Compute is modest (training SSMs on standard benchmarks fits a few GPUs). Both real and complex SSM variants already exist (e.g., S4 complex, Mamba real), so the comparison is implementable and incremental — no fundamental breakthrough needed. The scope is focused (compare two parameterizations across a fixed set of modalities), and evaluation uses standard metrics (accuracy, perplexity). The main difficulty is diagnostic (understanding why complex helps continuous data), which raises the bar slightly above a trivial ablation but still well within what a small team can address empirically.
